policy: A documented alias is two or more equipment definitions that share one realistic asset because they are the same physical object. It is permitted only while every aliased definition keeps a distinct label and accessible name, so the visible and screen-reader semantics stay separate. An undocumented shared asset is a lint failure; a documented alias must not be "fixed" by generating distinct art. Ungraduated stock-size variants may reuse a bottle-family silhouette as an illustrative icon when their distinct capacity and accessible label are explicit; this is not a claim that the two capacities have identical physical dimensions.

aliases.rationale: A waste beaker is a 250 mL beaker designated for waste. The designation is procedural, not physical, so the art is correctly shared.
The phenolphthalein dropper is the same physical dropper bottle carrying a named reagent.

One reagent-bottle body serves the generic bottle, the 0.100 M NaOH stock, and the unknown acid. The contents differ; the glassware does not. The 1 L stock variant uses this ungraduated family silhouette with an explicit 1 L label and independent capacity.

Ungraded bottle-family silhouette; volume is computed from the distinct equipment capacity, not inferred from the icon dimensions. The 1 L stock variant uses this ungraduated family silhouette with an explicit 1 L label and independent capacity.
